correctness.rationale: The difference multiplier is invertible on the one missing real Fourier plane, yielding an antipodally paired cosine gradient. Nullspace strict inequality gives uniform uniqueness, and a balanced opposing-sign gradient attains converse failure including the equality boundary. Between ordering/zero breakpoints the concentration quotient is fractional linear in sine/cosine with constant derivative sign, so phase extrema are at multiples of pi/n and reduce to the two phases modulo 2pi/n. The top-s order-statistic variational identity and uniform Riemann sums prove the sine limiting share and 1/3 critical density. The standalone checker passed 89056 finite tests; these do not substitute for analytic proof.

value.rationale: A single lost conjugate Fourier pair is the minimal nontrivial real spectral erasure; the result gives an exact finite-size all-signal recovery test across all primitive frequencies and identifies a sharp macroscopic one-third jump-density boundary. This directly quantifies resilience of convex cyclic-edge sparse reconstruction and supplies explicit adversarial counterexamples. Both the two-phase simplification and limiting threshold are more than a routine use of a generic nullspace inequality.
